seoTitle: Add a Calendar to Your Hostinger Website
metaDescription: Embed Google Calendar or another scheduling tool into your Hostinger website using the Website Builder's Embed Code element.
intro: Whether you're running a blog, business site, or booking platform, embedding a calendar on your Hostinger website helps visitors see your availability or upcoming events at a glance, and you don't need a developer or a paid plugin to do it. This guide covers getting from your Hostinger dashboard into the Website Builder's element panel, finding the embed option that accepts a calendar's code, and where to grab that code from Google Calendar in the first place.

steps.heading: Open your Websites list in hPanel
steps.body: After logging in, you land on Websites inside hPanel, which lists every site tied to your account under its hosting plan — in this case a Cloud Startup plan showing several sites, each with its own status. A domain that's temporary or not yet connected is flagged directly in the list, like "Domain not connected" with a Check guide link, so you can confirm the right site is fully set up before trying to edit it. Find the site you want to add a calendar to and use the Edit website or Tools option next to it.

image.caption: The Websites list in hPanel, showing connected sites with their domains and quick actions like Edit website and Tools.

steps.heading: Open the element panel in Website Builder
steps.body: Inside Website Builder, click Add section (or the plus icon) to open the panel of building blocks you can drop onto the page — Text, Button, Add to bag, Image, Gallery, Video, Shape, Map, Instagram feed, Contact form (RSVP), Subscription form, and Social icons all sit in the same grid. Below those, a code icon labeled for embedding raw code is what you're actually after for a calendar, since Hostinger doesn't have a dedicated "Calendar" block — it works by accepting embed code from an external calendar service instead.

image.caption: The Website Builder's element panel, with content blocks like Contact form, Subscription form, and an embed-code option near the bottom.

steps.heading: Get your calendar's embed code from Google Calendar
steps.body: Outside of Hostinger, open Google Calendar's own Settings, select the specific calendar you want to display — shown here as a calendar named "PMN Online" with its time zone set to India Standard Time and an Owner field confirming who controls it — and look for the Integrate calendar section. That section provides an embed code you copy in full; the same settings page is also where you'd rename the calendar, add a description, or export it if you ever need a backup.

image.caption: Google Calendar's settings page for a specific calendar, including its name, time zone, and owner, near where the embed code lives.

steps.heading: Paste the code into the Embed element
steps.body: Back in Hostinger's Website Builder, place the embed-code element on the page where you want the calendar to show, click into it, and paste the code you copied from Google Calendar. The same embed element works for other calendar and booking tools too — Apple Calendar, Microsoft Outlook Calendar, and third-party booking widgets like those from Booking.com all provide their own embed codes in a similar format, so this one element covers more than just Google's calendar.

steps.heading: Resize and reposition the calendar block
steps.body: Once pasted, the calendar renders directly on the page as a live, interactive component rather than a static image. Drag its edges to resize it, or move the whole block to a different section of the page if it doesn't fit well where you first placed it — a full-width placement near the top of a booking or events page tends to read better than squeezing it into a narrow sidebar column.

steps.heading: Save and publish the change
steps.body: Use Save to keep your progress inside the builder, then Update website (or Publish, depending on your builder version) to push the calendar live on your actual domain. Preview the page afterward on both desktop and mobile view, since embedded calendars can render narrower than expected on small screens and sometimes need a manual width adjustment to stay usable there.

steps.heading: Confirm the right domain is connected
steps.body: If your site's domain shows as temporary or not connected, as flagged in the Websites list, get that resolved before relying on the calendar being visible to real visitors — a calendar embedded on a temporary builder-preview URL won't be seen by anyone browsing your actual domain. Once the domain shows connected, revisit the live page one more time to confirm the calendar loads correctly outside of the builder's preview mode.

faq.question: Which calendar services can I embed in Hostinger?
faq.answer: Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Microsoft Outlook Calendar, and third-party booking widgets can all be embedded using the same embed-code element in Website Builder.

faq.question: Do I need coding skills to add a calendar?
faq.answer: No, you just need the embed code provided by your calendar service's own settings, which you paste into Hostinger's embed-code element without writing anything yourself.

faq.question: Can visitors book appointments through the embedded calendar?
faq.answer: This depends on the calendar or booking tool you embed — some services support interactive booking directly through the widget, while a plain Google Calendar embed is mainly for viewing availability.

faq.question: Where do I find the embed code for Google Calendar?
faq.answer: In Google Calendar's Settings for the specific calendar you want to share, under the Integrate calendar section, where an embed code is provided for you to copy.

faq.question: What if my calendar doesn't show up after publishing?
faq.answer: Check that your site's domain is fully connected rather than still on a temporary builder-preview URL, since a calendar added while the domain isn't connected won't be visible to visitors on your real website.
